## Elements of code

There are different terms for different elements of code

```{r}
#| eval: false
data |>
  select(
    species,
    island
  )
```

:::: {.fragment}
In the above code:

::: {.incremental}
- `data` is an object
- `select` is a function
- `species` and `island` are arguments of the `select` function
:::
::::

## Assignment (`<-`)

R prints results in the console by default

::: {.fragment}
```{r}
#| output: true
read_csv("data/penguins.csv")
```

:::

::: {.fragment}
Assign results using `<-` to store in an object

```{r}
data <- read_csv("data/penguins.csv")
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
The shortcut for the assignment operator is `Alt + -` or `Option + -`
:::

## Accessing elements of an object

Sometimes we need to access one element of an object, such as a single column in our data

::: {.fragment}
We can do this using `$` or `[""]`

```{r}
#| eval: false
data$species

data["species"]
```
:::
::: {.fragment}
This is not always required, such as in the context of pipes
:::

## Pipes (`|>`)

Chain sequences of functions together using pipes

::: {.fragment}

```{r}
#| eval: false
data <- read_csv("data/penguins.csv")
data <- filter(data, species == "Chinstrap")
data <- mutate(data,
               body_mass_kg = body_mass/1000)
summarise(data, mean_body_mass = mean(body_mass_kg))
```
:::

::: {.fragment}
Pipes effectively fill in the first argument of a function:

```{r}
#| eval: false
data <- read_csv("data/penguins.csv")
data |>
  filter(species == "Chinstrap") |>
  mutate(body_mass_kg = body_mass/1000) |>
  summarise(mean_body_mass = mean(body_mass_kg))
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
The shortcut for the pipe operator is `Ctrl + Shift + M`
:::

## Keyboard shortcuts

To see all keyboard shortcuts, click on 'Keyboard Shortcuts Help' in the 'Help' menu 

My most commonly used are:

- Insert pipe (`Ctrl + Shift + M`)
- Insert assignment operator (`Option/Alt + -`)
- Move line up or down (`Option/Alt + Up/Down`)
- Duplicate line or selection (`Cmd + Option + Up/Down`)
- Delete line or selection (`Cmd + D`)
- Comment or uncomment (`Cmd + Shift + C`)

## Common types of things

::: {.incremental}
- Numbers and integers
- Logicals
- Factors (<https://forcats.tidyverse.org/>)
- Dates/times (<https://lubridate.tidyverse.org/>)
- Characters (<https://stringr.tidyverse.org/>)
- Missing
- Vectors and lists
- Data frames and tibbles (<https://tibble.tidyverse.org/>)

:::

## Missing

Missing has its own special identity in R — `NA`

```{r}
penguin_species <- c("Adelie", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap", NA)
penguin_species
```

::: {.fragment}
It also has its own special function to check if something is missing:

```{r}
is.na(penguin_species)
```
:::

::: {.fragment}
Be sure to use `is.na()`, if you just use the equals operator it won't work:

```{r}
penguin_species == NA
```
:::

## Human-readable code

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Example
```{r}
#| eval: false
data |> mutate(ldr=bill_len/bill_dep)
```

### Space
```{r}
#| eval: false
data |> mutate(ldr = bill_len / bill_dep)
```

### Lines
```{r}
#| eval: false
data |> 
  mutate(
    ldr = bill_len / bill_dep
  )
```

### Naming
```{r}
#| eval: false
data |> 
  mutate(
    length_depth_ratio = bill_len / bill_dep
  )
```

### Comments
```{r}
#| eval: false
data |> 
  mutate(
    # Calculate the bill length/depth ratio
    length_depth_ratio = bill_len / bill_dep
  )
```

### Bookmarks
```{r}
#| eval: false
#### Cleaning ####
data |> 
  mutate(
    # Calculate the bill length/depth ratio
    length_depth_ratio = bill_len / bill_dep
  )

#### Plots ####
ggplot(
  ⋮
```
:::


::: {.callout-tip}
Formatters like `air` do a lot of the work for you <https://tidyverse.org/blog/2025/02/air/>
:::

## Common errors

::: {.panel-tabset}
### Trailing comma
```{r}
#| error: true
penguin_species <- c(
  "Adelie", 
  "Gentoo", 
  "Chinstrap",
  )
```

### Missing comma
```{r}
#| error: true
penguin_species <- c(
  "Adelie"
  "Gentoo"
  "Chinstrap"
  )
```

### Equals signs
```{r}
#| error: true
data |> 
  mutate(
    is_chinstrap = species = "Chinstrap"
  )
```

### Unclosed bracket
```{r}
#| error: true
data |> 
  mutate(
    is_chinstrap = species == "Chinstrap"
    
ggplot(data)
```

### Too many brackets
```{r}
#| error: true
data |> 
  mutate(
    is_chinstrap = species == "Chinstrap"
  )
)
```
:::

## Error messages

They try to tell you what the problem was, but it's not always easy

1. Read the error message
1. Look at your code
2. Read help files
3. Check for cheatsheets
4. Web search
5. Join a community
6. Ask an LLM

Try to figure out the solution yourself before consulting an LLM, you'll learn more!

::: {.callout-tip}
You'll get lots of error messages as you learn how to code, this is normal
:::
